messages:
Rina Kobayashi: seeing a p95 regression in one mixed scenario. quick heads up before we burn more canary cycles.

Rina Kobayashi: scenario: `mix_trace_c3` (70% short chat, 30% long summarization). model `llama-3-70b` on A100-80GB. baseline vs sched-flag-on.

Rina Kobayashi: excerpt:
```
        baseline     flag_on
p50_e2e   118ms       121ms
p95_e2e   612ms       742ms   (+21%)
p99_e2e  1190ms      1315ms   (+10%)
through  1.00x       0.97x
```

Rina Kobayashi: p95 only regresses when long prompts present. pure-short scenario is fine (actually a bit better).

Marcus Reed: ugh. do we see queue depth weirdness or is it mostly service time?

Rina Kobayashi: dashboards show short-queue wait spikes. not huge backlog overall, more like short requests getting stuck behind “long prefill batch windows”.

Lena Fischer: that sounds like misclassification (short incorrectly tagged long -> ends up in long queue and gets serviced in bursts), or priority inversion bug (short tagged short but still blocked).

Omar El-Sayed: do we have the per-request classifier labels in the benchmark output? (even sampled)

Rina Kobayashi: not currently. runner only emits pXX + queue metrics. i can add logs but it’ll take a bit.

Sofia Ivanova: can we reproduce w/ debug build and turn on sampled structured logs? (PR 8502 isn’t merged yet but we can locally patch)

Marcus Reed: we do have the temporary `RUNTIME_SCHED_DEBUG=1` trace events from PR 8444. should include `class=short|long` at enqueue + dequeue.

Julian Moore: ^ yeah, trace spans include `sched.classification.bucket` and `sched.classification.reason` (threshold vs fallback). only in perf builds though.

Omar El-Sayed: if it’s mislabeling, we should see short requests with small prompt_tokens going to long queue. what’s the threshold right now?

Marcus Reed: config default is `prompt_tokens >= 2048 => long` (plus a stub “predicted prefill” if available). streaming not special-cased.

Lena Fischer: any chance the “prompt_tokens” count includes system prompt + tool schema? those can be big in the trace.

Rina Kobayashi: possible. trace has some tool-heavy routes. but this scenario was supposed to be representative of “chat + periodic summarization” where chat includes tool schema.

Jonas Weber: do we have the prompt length distribution for the short class in this trace? if lots of “short chat” is actually 2k-3k tokens due to tool schema, we might be pushing those into long.

Samir Qureshi: another angle: classifier uses prompt tokens only, but long requests are prefill-heavy. short requests are decode-heavy. if chat has big prompt but small output, maybe treating it as long is correct? but then policy should still protect interactive.

Lena Fischer: right, but our “short” definition in the policy is “latency-sensitive”, not “short prompt”. we’re approximating with prompt length. tool-schema chat is latency-sensitive but looks long. that’s a known failure mode.

Sofia Ivanova: ok, let’s separate:
1) bug (short blocked behind long prefill batch)
2) expected tradeoff due to heuristic mismatch (tool-heavy chat)

Sofia Ivanova: Rina, can you run two experiments:
- A: force classifier threshold to something huge (e.g. 8192) so almost everything is “short” except true long summarization
- B: force everything to FIFO (disable two-queue, keep instrumentation) if possible

Rina Kobayashi: can do A easily via config. B needs a build toggle; but I can run baseline (flag off) which is basically FIFO.

Marcus Reed: for A, we should also try threshold lower (1024) to see if it correlates. if p95 worsens monotonically, it’s classification-driven.

Omar El-Sayed: also add a quick derived metric from traces: % of requests in short queue with prompt_tokens > 2048, and % in long queue with prompt_tokens < 512. if we see a bunch of the latter, it’s definitely wrong.

Julian Moore: we can do that with trace post-processing. if Rina can upload the trace json, I can hack a small parser.

Rina Kobayashi: i can re-run with tracing enabled and attach the trace artifact. (will be big). where do you want it?

Julian Moore: drop in the shared drive folder for perf artifacts (same one as last week). ping me link.

Grace Kim: kernel side question: did anything change between baseline and flag-on that could affect kernel selection? (batching patterns can shift which kernels get picked)

Marcus Reed: no kernel changes, but scheduler changes batching/dispatch order so kernel selection could differ indirectly.

Grace Kim: ok. would be good to confirm we’re not accidentally creating giant prefill batches that pick a slower kernel variant.

Omar El-Sayed: we should check prefill/decode split metrics. do we have prefill time histograms by class?

Rina Kobayashi: only aggregate prefill/decode p95. i can extend the bench runner to break out by class next, but for now traces should show.

Jonas Weber: do we see the regression on both A100 and H100?

Rina Kobayashi: only ran A100 so far. I can queue H100 once we know what to look for.

Sofia Ivanova: next steps:
- Rina: rerun `mix_trace_c3` with threshold=8192 and threshold=1024 + tracing enabled (same seed)
- Julian/Omar: parse traces for mislabeling indicators + time spent waiting behind prefill batches
- Marcus/Lena: sanity check policy config defaults for tool-heavy chat (maybe we need a “latency-sensitive hint” from route metadata, even if it’s just a temporary allowlist in benchmark)

Marcus Reed: ack. I’ll also double-check we’re not doing “drain long queue for N batches” when long queue has a single monster request. could cause these bursts.

Lena Fischer: if it’s tool-schema chat, we may need a second heuristic: use expected output tokens / streaming flag / route tier. even a conservative override like `if streaming => short` might fix most.

Samir Qureshi: careful: streaming can still have huge prompt prefill cost; but yeah, product-wise streaming is interactive.

Omar El-Sayed: +1 to treating streaming as latency-sensitive. we can cap how much long work we admit while streaming backlog exists.

Rina Kobayashi: will kick runs now. ETA ~2h for both configs.

Marcus Reed: :thumbsup:

(DeployBot): :information_source: perf-lab job queued by @rina.kobayashi: `mix_trace_c3` (A100) configs: threshold=8192, threshold=1024, tracing=on.

Rina Kobayashi: link to artifacts (traces + raw metrics): https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1tqK7xq9-perf-mixc3 (internal)

Julian Moore: grabbed. initial quick scan: long queue has a bunch of requests with `prompt_tokens ~ 2300-2600` and `max_new_tokens=64`, streaming=true. those are likely chat/tool calls.

Omar El-Sayed: that’s our smoking gun. those are “prompt-long” but not “latency-insensitive”.

Lena Fischer: yep. with threshold=8192 those stay in short queue -> p95 should improve.

Rina Kobayashi: results came back:
```
threshold=8192
p95_e2e  590ms (better than baseline)
through  0.99x

threshold=1024
p95_e2e  811ms (worse)
through  0.96x
```

Rina Kobayashi: so it’s strongly classification-driven.

Sofia Ivanova: great isolation. action item: add a “streaming => short” override (or more generally “latency_sensitive => short”) for prototype. and in benchmarks, label routes that are interactive.

Marcus Reed: I can do a minimal change: if `request.streaming == true` and `max_new_tokens <= 256` then classify as short even if prompt_tokens > threshold. behind flag.

Grace Kim: if that shifts dispatch patterns, please re-run the kernel selection diff after. but this looks correct.

Jonas Weber: also update the perf standard notes: prompt-length heuristic alone is insufficient when tool schema inflates prompts.

Sofia Ivanova: cool. Marcus file a PR + add regression test in the perf suite for tool-schema chat. Rina, can you keep these artifacts for the design review? (this is exactly the “failure mode” slide)

Rina Kobayashi: yep will link in the project notes.

Omar El-Sayed: I’ll add a small panel request to the dashboards spec: % streaming requests classified long, alert if >X%.

Julian Moore: +1. also we should store `classification_reason` in metrics so we can see how often overrides fire.

Sofia Ivanova: closing loop here. next check-in tomorrow after PR is up + rerun suite.

Marcus Reed: on it.
